clue.text: Many in tatters lagged behind

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for a large number
something in tatters is torn and ragged

explanation.surface: A crowd of people in rags straggled along behind the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail along slowly at the rear is to have dragged one's feet.

clue.text: Diana's the girl to make cashier

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, plus the possessive S
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Diana is the young woman chosen to work the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a noun for a bank clerk; here it is the verb meaning to sack someone, especially from the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to expel them from service, to sack or discharge them.

clue.text: After midnight draw on a flask

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the hours after midnight, ante meridiem
to draw a cart is to pull it

explanation.surface: In the small hours someone takes a swig from a hip flask.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla is a small round flask, as used in ancient Rome or for holy oil.

clue.text: Major causing the old king to scoff

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on old postboxes
to scoff in British slang is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Some important matter has made a former monarch gobble his food.
explanation.definitionFit: Major and great are synonyms meaning large or important.

clue.text: Strip the underworld guy, then let off

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the underworld itself
a guy is a man

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gangster from the underworld is stripped and then released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' could be a noun, but it is the verb, to take apart. 'off' gives TLE, the anagram of LET; 'then' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it apart, to strip it down.

clue.text: Quiet women perhaps, but they're exhibitionists

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible rearrangement of the letters of women

explanation.surface: Quiet women, you might think, but in fact they love to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits after 'perhaps', but that word is the anagram signal, making OWMEN; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Showmen are flamboyant performers who love an audience, much like people who show off.

clue.text: A screen riddle

explanation.surface: A puzzle on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is not a puzzle here but a coarse sieve, and as a verb to riddle is to sift.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a mesh screen for separating, and a riddle is a coarse strainer for soil or grain.

clue.text: Top men reading love poetry without hesitation

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the poetry goes around the hesitation

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Bosses recite romantic verse smoothly, without stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking, so the poetry goes round the hesitation. 'reading' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervisors in charge of workers are the bosses at the top of a workplace.

clue.text: Swallow a single cocktail

parts.note: the house martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone downs just one mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Not existing in any locale or doubly present?

parts.note: present in time means now, and present in place means here: two senses of the one word
the second sense of present, being at this place

explanation.surface: A riddle about something absent everywhere yet present twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Not existing in any place at all is to be in no place whatever.

clue.text: Step back before minor, lacking spirit

indicators.note: back tells us the word for the step is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pas is a step in ballet
minor means smaller or less

explanation.surface: A dancer steps back in front of a lesser performer, without energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step' is the French ballet term; 'back' turns it into SAP. 'minor' is an adjective meaning smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapless means without sap, so feeble and without vigour.

clue.text: It's topping for the viewer!

parts.note: the viewer is an eye, and the topping is the arch of hair above it

explanation.surface: An excited review of a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' seems to mean excellent and 'viewer' a TV audience; read literally, it is hair sitting on top of an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above each eye sits on top of the organ of sight.

clue.text: The italian left a kid in some discomfort

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: An Italian man left a young goat in some distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a young goat or child; it is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uncomfortable or uneasy is a state of unease.

clue.text: Beastly creatures -a quarter drink

parts.note: S for south is one of the four compass points, a quarter of the compass
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Unpleasant animals put away a quarter of the booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine are pigs, and the word is also used for nasty people.

clue.text: Support for those in office

explanation.surface: Help for office workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a walking stick that holds you up, and also the employees of an organisation.

clue.text: Irresolute fellow changing

parts.note: changing means altering

explanation.surface: A man who keeps changing his mind is indecisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wavering and hesitant is indecisive, unsure what to do.

clue.text: May be tried and seen to get less tough

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A case may go to trial and be heard, so the treatment is softened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' rearranges the letters of TRIED and SEEN together; 'and' only joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenderise meat is to soften it so that it becomes less chewy.

clue.text: Men turn it (when properly cooked) into wholesome food

indicators.note: cooked in the sense of reworked, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cooks turn food properly to make a healthy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when properly cooked' rearranges MEN TURN IT; 'into' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, food that sustains the body.

clue.text: Some serving men save, remember!

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to save up money or stamps is to collect them

explanation.surface: An order to soldiers to save their pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to call something back to mind.

clue.text: Making about a hundred pounds, intend to save

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone earning around a hundred pounds means to put it aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim land or materials is to rescue them for use, to save them.

clue.text: Caught over hustle, gets reprimand

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to hustle is to hurry, to hasten

explanation.surface: A man caught running in a hurry is told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten someone is to rebuke or discipline them.

clue.text: Make a start and there's contention

explanation.surface: Getting going and having an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to is to begin work in earnest, and a set-to is a fight or quarrel.

clue.text: A woman has to adjust her seat

indicators.note: adjust means rearrange, here the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A lady needs to move her chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to adjust' rearranges HER SEAT; 'has' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Shocking the old boy with a bit of play

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: A former pupil is appalled by part of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscene is offensive and outrageous to decency.

clue.text: About to go on the box

indicators.note: in an across clue on means coming after, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: C stands for circa, meaning about
rate as in going rate or speed, how fast something goes

explanation.surface: Someone is about to appear on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' suggests the television; the definition is a plain packing case.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden packing case.

clue.text: Yet the head appears calm

parts.note: still means yet, as in still waiting
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: Even so, the boss looks unruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss or a person's head; it is a promontory, as in place names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Stillness is quiet and tranquillity, the absence of motion.

clue.text: The children will pocket cash and run!

indicators.note: pocket means put inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
P for penny is a small unit of cash

explanation.surface: Kids will grab the money and dash off.
explanation.definitionFit: To run is to move with haste, to go fast.

clue.text: Some, a handful, ate right afterwards

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, picked out from inside the words

explanation.surface: A few people ate properly later on.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text reads 'night', but the run needs 'right': handfuL ATE Right.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and afterwards both mean at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Trade is bad, though up

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of the two words are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Business is poor, though prices are rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like rising trade; it means mounted on a horse, sitting with a leg on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider up on a horse sits astride it, legs either side.

clue.text: Unreasonable in the end

explanation.surface: Being irrational at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means excessive or immoderate, and also furthest out or final, as in the extreme tip.

clue.text: Being elderly, was successful

parts.note: a man is a human being
aged means elderly

explanation.surface: Being old, someone did well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a participle meaning existing; it is a noun, a person.
explanation.definitionFit: If you managed to do something, you coped and pulled it off.

clue.text: Row of houses built of earth by engineer

parts.note: terra is Latin for earth
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Homes built of mud by an engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a line of joined houses, common in British streets.
